TEXT.source: kanakanavu.info, "S. Tsuchida 2003 Story 3", https://kanakanavu.info/language-documentation/s-tsuchida-2003-story-3.html. This story was originally recorded by Shigeru Tsuchida in February 1969. The speaker is Angaiana Paa’u. The original transcription and analysis are published in Tsuchida, Shigeru (2003). Kanakanavu Texts (Austronesian Formosan). Osaka: Osaka Gakuin University (Endangered Languages of the Pacific Rim Publications Series A3-014).

S.FORM: tee-pa ku puumuamuarʉ puiisua sua ni-arupakarʉ'ʉ mata ngkou.
S.PHON: teepa ku puumuamua[r|ɾ]ɨ puiisua sua nia[r|ɾ]upaka[r|ɾ]ɨʔɨ mata ŋkou
S.FORM: teepa ku puumuamuarʉ puiisua sua niarupakarʉ'ʉ mata ngkou.
S.PHON: teepa ku puumuamua[r|ɾ]ɨ puiisua sua nia[r|ɾ]upaka[r|ɾ]ɨʔɨ mata ŋkou
S.TRANSL: I will be talking about the one who was in love with a monkey.
I'm going to talk about the one who loved monkey with each other.

S.FORM: sua kani ngaca-in ia necu'u sua matata na kana-minmina.
S.PHON: sua kani ŋaʦain ia neʦuʔu sua matata na kanaminmina
S.FORM: sua kani ngacain ia necu'u sua matata na kanaminmina.
S.PHON: sua kani ŋaʦain ia neʦuʔu sua matata na kanaminmina
S.TRANSL: As for the base (of the story), it refers to the happening of scaring birds coincidently.
The story begins from the season of scaring birds.

S.FORM: 'una sua kinvara nanakʉ mata saronei.
S.PHON: ʔuna sua kinva[r|ɾ]a nanakɨ mata sa[r|ɾ]onei
S.FORM: 'una sua kinvara nanakʉ mata saronei.
S.PHON: ʔuna sua kinva[r|ɾ]a nanakɨ mata sa[r|ɾ]onei
S.TRANSL: There were sibilings, a female and a male one.
有兄弟，一個人是男的， 一個女的。
There were a woman and a man who were sister and brother to each other.

S.FORM: sua nanakʉ ia tantantaniarʉ maamia mukusa 'inia minana.
S.PHON: sua nanakɨ ia tantantania[r|ɾ]ɨ maamia mukusa ʔinia minana
S.FORM: sua nanakʉ ia tantantaniarʉ maamia mukusa 'inia minana.
S.PHON: sua nanakɨ ia tantantania[r|ɾ]ɨ maamia mukusa ʔinia minana
S.TRANSL: As for the female, she went every day chasing birds away.
The woman went to scare birds everyday.

S.FORM: natee kani 'apanap-ʉn saronei pu'iri mukusa 'inia minana,
S.PHON: natee kani ʔapanapɨn sa[r|ɾ]onei puʔi[r|ɾ]i mukusa ʔinia minana
S.FORM: natee kani 'apanapʉn saronei pu'iri mukusa 'inia minana,
S.PHON: natee kani ʔapanapɨn sa[r|ɾ]onei puʔi[r|ɾ]i mukusa ʔinia minana
S.TRANSL: Originally the man sometimes tried to switch to chase the birds,
Originally the man sometimes tried to fill in to chase the birds,
The man sometimes proposed to go there to scare birds.

S.FORM: nakai ka'aan pakituru sua nanakʉ.
S.PHON: nakai kaʔaan pakitu[r|ɾ]u sua nanakɨ
S.FORM: nakai ka'aan pakituru sua nanakʉ.
S.PHON: nakai kaʔaan pakitu[r|ɾ]u sua nanakɨ
S.TRANSL: but the woman did not allow it.
But the woman did not allow.

S.FORM: makasua cu sua saronei paravou tee pa cu kʉcʉ pu'iri mukusa 'inia misei.
S.PHON: makasua ʦu sua sa[r|ɾ]onei pa[r|ɾ]avou tee pa ʦu kɨʦɨ puʔi[r|ɾ]i mukusa ʔinia misei
S.FORM: makasua cu sua saronei paravou tee pa cu kʉcʉ pu'iri mukusa 'inia misei.
S.PHON: makasua ʦu sua sa[r|ɾ]onei pa[r|ɾ]avou tee pa ʦu kɨʦɨ puʔi[r|ɾ]i mukusa ʔinia misei
S.TRANSL: Therefore the man said: " Let's try, I will fill in and go!" he said.
Therefore the man tried, "I'll dare to change and go there," said he.

S.FORM: mu-puara kan pitʉ'a mukusa 'inia.
S.PHON: mupua[r|ɾ]a kan pitɨʔa mukusa ʔinia
S.FORM: mupuara kan pitʉ'a mukusa 'inia.
S.PHON: mupua[r|ɾ]a kan pitɨʔa mukusa ʔinia
S.TRANSL: He left in the dark to go there.
He left very early in the morning to go there.

S.FORM: makacukʉna kan inia na tamina.
S.PHON: makaʦukɨna kan inia na tamina
S.FORM: makacukʉna kan inia na tamina.
S.PHON: makaʦukɨna kan inia na tamina
S.TRANSL: He arrived at the place of chasing birds.
He arrived at the place of scaring birds.

S.FORM: mari'anʉ marikʉvʉ sʉrʉʉcʉ kan inia sua ngkou taparacici 'inia.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]iʔanɨ ma[r|ɾ]ikɨvɨ sɨ[r|ɾ]ɨɨʦɨ kan inia sua ŋkou tapa[r|ɾ]aʦiʦi ʔinia
S.FORM: mari'anʉ marikʉvʉ sʉrʉʉcʉ kan inia sua ngkou taparacici 'inia.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]iʔanɨ ma[r|ɾ]ikɨvɨ sɨ[r|ɾ]ɨɨʦɨ kan inia sua ŋkou tapa[r|ɾ]aʦiʦi ʔinia
S.TRANSL: He clapped once. A single monkey appeared.
He pulled the clapper once. A solitary monkey appeared.

S.FORM: pana-'ei kan inia sua ngkou um-ara um-avici tanasa.
S.PHON: panaʔei kan inia sua ŋkou uma[r|ɾ]a umaviʦi tanasa
S.FORM: pana'ei kan inia sua ngkou umara umavici tanasa.
S.PHON: panaʔei kan inia sua ŋkou uma[r|ɾ]a umaviʦi tanasa
S.TRANSL: He shot the monkey. He took it and brought it home.
He shot the monkey. He took it and brought it home.

S.FORM: makasua cu tee kan cu kaa'ara'araam kei sua ngkou.
S.PHON: makasua ʦu tee kan ʦu kaaʔa[r|ɾ]aʔa[r|ɾ]aam kei sua ŋkou
S.FORM: makasua cu tee kan cu kaa'ara'araam kei sua ngkou.
S.PHON: makasua ʦu tee kan ʦu kaaʔa[r|ɾ]aʔa[r|ɾ]aam kei sua ŋkou
S.TRANSL: Then, he made meat from the monkey.
Then he cut the monkey into meats.

S.FORM: taka'isua kan sua nanakʉ tupuru na tapari'ʉvʉa si 'esi aka cʉpʉng-ini.
S.PHON: takaʔisua kan sua nanakɨ tupu[r|ɾ]u na tapa[r|ɾ]iʔɨvɨa si ʔesi aka ʦɨpɨŋini
S.FORM: taka'isua kan sua nanakʉ tupuru na tapari'ʉvʉa si 'esi aka cʉpʉngini.
S.PHON: takaʔisua kan sua nanakɨ tupu[r|ɾ]u na tapa[r|ɾ]iʔɨvɨa si ʔesi aka ʦɨpɨŋini
S.TRANSL: The woman ? sat at the smoking place because she was sad.
The woman, telling a lie, sat at the smoky place, because she was very sad.

S.FORM: marasinsinʉka kani 'esi kia pa ʉvʉ-'ʉn misa kani si 'esi aka cʉpʉng-ini c<um>ʉra 'acu ni-pana'a naa-karʉ-'e-in.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]asinsinɨka kani ʔesi kia pa ɨvɨʔɨn misa kani si ʔesi aka ʦɨpɨŋini ʦumɨ[r|ɾ]a ʔaʦu nipanaʔa naaka[r|ɾ]ɨʔein
S.FORM: marasinsinʉka kani 'esi kia pa ʉvʉ'ʉn misa kani si 'esi aka cʉpʉngini cumʉra 'acu nipana'a naakarʉ'ein.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]asinsinɨka kani ʔesi kia pa ɨvɨʔɨn misa kani si ʔesi aka ʦɨpɨŋini ʦumɨ[r|ɾ]a ʔaʦu nipanaʔa naaka[r|ɾ]ɨʔein
S.TRANSL: She sobbed. "I am still smoking", she said, since she was sad seeing her lover has been shot.
She sobbed. 'Tm being smoked," she said, because she was sad because her lover had been shot.

S.FORM: 'esi ava tarapaapa-'ʉn kei sua 'esi kaa'ara'aram ngkou sua ni-kuung-in inia.
S.PHON: ʔesi ava ta[r|ɾ]apaapaʔɨn kei sua ʔesi kaaʔa[r|ɾ]aʔa[r|ɾ]am ŋkou sua nikuuŋin inia
S.FORM: 'esi ava tarapaapa'ʉn kei sua 'esi kaa'ara'aram ngkou sua nikuungin inia.
S.PHON: ʔesi ava ta[r|ɾ]apaapaʔɨn kei sua ʔesi kaaʔa[r|ɾ]aʔa[r|ɾ]am ŋkou sua nikuuŋin inia
S.TRANSL: She suspiciously watched the one who made meat out of the monkey and stored it at some higher place.
She was looking askance the one who was cutting the monkey into meat which was stored at a high place.

S.FORM: makasua cu arapapiningi cu sua saronei paki'ama'amat-ei cu 'inia um-ara sua 'utingi ngkou masuvuku.
S.PHON: makasua ʦu a[r|ɾ]apapiniŋi ʦu sua sa[r|ɾ]onei pakiʔamaʔamatei ʦu ʔinia uma[r|ɾ]a sua ʔutiŋi ŋkou masuvuku
S.FORM: makasua cu arapapiningi cu sua saronei paki'ama'amatei cu 'inia umara sua 'utingi ngkou masuvuku.
S.PHON: makasua ʦu a[r|ɾ]apapiniŋi ʦu sua sa[r|ɾ]onei pakiʔamaʔamatei ʦu ʔinia uma[r|ɾ]a sua ʔutiŋi ŋkou masuvuku
S.TRANSL: Then, when that man went outside, she secretly took the monkey's penis and put it on the belt.
So, when the man went out, she secretly took the penis of the monkey and stuck it at the belt.

S.FORM: makasua cu takutavaraei cu kʉkʉnang-in.
S.PHON: makasua ʦu takutava[r|ɾ]aei ʦu kɨkɨnaŋin
S.FORM: makasua cu takutavaraei cu kʉkʉnangin.
S.PHON: makasua ʦu takutava[r|ɾ]aei ʦu kɨkɨnaŋin
S.TRANSL: Then, ther companions noticed it.
Later, ther companions noticed it.
Then her friends perceived it.

S.FORM: 'esi ava ni-pasuvuku kei sua uting ngkou misei.
S.PHON: ʔesi ava nipasuvuku kei sua utiŋ ŋkou misei
S.FORM: 'esi ava nipasuvuku kei sua uting ngkou misei.
S.PHON: ʔesi ava nipasuvuku kei sua utiŋ ŋkou misei
S.TRANSL: "We are wondering if she is having the monkey's penis at her belt." they said.
They said, "She is wearing the penis of a monkey at her belt"'.

S.FORM: arivicei cu kʉkʉnang-ini mukusa cakʉranʉ makananguru.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]iviʦei ʦu kɨkɨnaŋini mukusa ʦakɨ[r|ɾ]anɨ makanaŋu[r|ɾ]u
S.FORM: arivicei cu kʉkʉnangini mukusa cakʉranʉ makananguru.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]iviʦei ʦu kɨkɨnaŋini mukusa ʦakɨ[r|ɾ]anɨ makanaŋu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: Her companions took her to the river for swimming.
Her friends took her to the river for swimming.

S.FORM: pakituru kani sua isua kipapa mukusa cakʉranʉ.
S.PHON: pakitu[r|ɾ]u kani sua isua kipapa mukusa ʦakɨ[r|ɾ]anɨ
S.FORM: pakituru kani sua isua kipapa mukusa cakʉranʉ.
S.PHON: pakitu[r|ɾ]u kani sua isua kipapa mukusa ʦakɨ[r|ɾ]anɨ
S.TRANSL: She agreed to follow them to the river.
She consented to go to the river.

S.FORM: natee kan ka'aan pakituru makananguru.
S.PHON: natee kan kaʔaan pakitu[r|ɾ]u makanaŋu[r|ɾ]u
S.FORM: natee kan ka'aan pakituru makananguru.
S.PHON: natee kan kaʔaan pakitu[r|ɾ]u makanaŋu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: But she did not agree to swim.
She did not want to swim.

S.FORM: ringring-ini kan kʉkʉnang-in.
S.PHON: [r|ɾ]iŋ[r|ɾ]iŋini kan kɨkɨnaŋin
S.FORM: ringringini kan kʉkʉnangin.
S.PHON: [r|ɾ]iŋ[r|ɾ]iŋini kan kɨkɨnaŋin
S.TRANSL: Her companions forced her to.
Her friends compelled her.

S.FORM: makasua cu sua ka'aan makananguru ia tia paticucuvung r<um>ʉcʉ cu canumu kison kan kei!
S.PHON: makasua ʦu sua kaʔaan makanaŋu[r|ɾ]u ia tia patiʦuʦuvuŋ [r|ɾ]umɨʦɨ ʦu ʦanumu kison kan kei
S.FORM: makasua cu sua ka'aan makananguru ia tia paticucuvung rumʉcʉ cu canumu kison kan kei!
S.PHON: makasua ʦu sua kaʔaan makanaŋu[r|ɾ]u ia tia patiʦuʦuvuŋ [r|ɾ]umɨʦɨ ʦu ʦanumu kison kan kei
S.TRANSL: Then they said: " The one who does not swim will be taken together and thrown into the water!"
'The one who does not swim will be carried up by everybody and thrown into the water," they said.

S.FORM: acu kani uruunu kei sua nakʉv-ini.
S.PHON: aʦu kani u[r|ɾ]uunu kei sua nakɨvini
S.FORM: acu kani uruunu kei sua nakʉvini.
S.PHON: aʦu kani u[r|ɾ]uunu kei sua nakɨvini
S.TRANSL: She took off her clothes.
She took off her clothing.

S.FORM: musutavʉrʉ kan cu canumu makananguru.
S.PHON: musutavɨ[r|ɾ]ɨ kan ʦu ʦanumu makanaŋu[r|ɾ]u
S.FORM: musutavʉrʉ kan cu canumu makananguru.
S.PHON: musutavɨ[r|ɾ]ɨ kan ʦu ʦanumu makanaŋu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: She jumped into the water to swim.
She jumped into the water to swim.

S.FORM: paki'amat-ei cu kʉkʉnang-ini c<um>'ʉra sua naa-ni-pasuvuku kei uting ngkou.
S.PHON: pakiʔamatei ʦu kɨkɨnaŋini ʦumʔɨ[r|ɾ]a sua naanipasuvuku kei utiŋ ŋkou
S.FORM: paki'amatei cu kʉkʉnangini cum'ʉra sua naanipasuvuku kei uting ngkou.
S.PHON: pakiʔamatei ʦu kɨkɨnaŋini ʦumʔɨ[r|ɾ]a sua naanipasuvuku kei utiŋ ŋkou
S.TRANSL: Secretly, her companions saw the hidden monkey penis stuck at her belt.
Without being noticed, her friends looked at the penis of the monkey stuck at her belt.

S.FORM: kurei ava cu misa kani.
S.PHON: ku[r|ɾ]ei ava ʦu misa kani
S.FORM: kurei ava cu misa kani.
S.PHON: ku[r|ɾ]ei ava ʦu misa kani
S.TRANSL: "Maggots!" they said.
"It's infested with maggots," they said.

S.FORM: ara-ei kan 'inia t<um>eini pitatavʉrʉ cu canumu apa-acun.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aei kan ʔinia tumeini pitatavɨ[r|ɾ]ɨ ʦu ʦanumu apaaʦun
S.FORM: araei kan 'inia tumeini pitatavʉrʉ cu canumu apaacun.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aei kan ʔinia tumeini pitatavɨ[r|ɾ]ɨ ʦu ʦanumu apaaʦun
S.TRANSL: They took it and threw it into the water and let it drift away.
They took it and threw it away into water to float away.

S.FORM: makasua cu tani'ura-ei cu 'inia sua nanakʉ.
S.PHON: makasua ʦu taniʔu[r|ɾ]aei ʦu ʔinia sua nanakɨ
S.FORM: makasua cu tani'uraei cu 'inia sua nanakʉ.
S.PHON: makasua ʦu taniʔu[r|ɾ]aei ʦu ʔinia sua nanakɨ
S.TRANSL: Later, they lied at the woman.
Then they cheated the woman.

S.FORM: taa cu 'isa cu cangini misei arakeikiou mucaan.
S.PHON: taa ʦu ʔisa ʦu ʦaŋini misei a[r|ɾ]akeikiou muʦaan
S.FORM: taa cu 'isa cu cangini misei arakeikiou mucaan.
S.PHON: taa ʦu ʔisa ʦu ʦaŋini misei a[r|ɾ]akeikiou muʦaan
S.TRANSL: "Let's go! Enemy is here!" They said and went away in a confused manner.
"Let's go! enemy came!" and went away confusedly.

S.FORM: 'eisi kan 'inia sua nanakʉ isua musuteini.
S.PHON: ʔeisi kan ʔinia sua nanakɨ isua musuteini
S.FORM: 'eisi kan 'inia sua nanakʉ isua musuteini.
S.PHON: ʔeisi kan ʔinia sua nanakɨ isua musuteini
S.TRANSL: The woman was left aside.
That woman was left behind.

S.FORM: tee kirikirim 'inia koo cu ʉtʉan-ei.
S.PHON: tee ki[r|ɾ]iki[r|ɾ]im ʔinia koo ʦu ɨtɨanei
S.FORM: tee kirikirim 'inia koo cu ʉtʉanei.
S.PHON: tee ki[r|ɾ]iki[r|ɾ]im ʔinia koo ʦu ɨtɨanei
S.TRANSL: She was looking for it (the penis), but she did not find.

TRANSL.notes: Tsuchida (2003) original free translation (OFTE line); it = penis

S.TRANSL: She looked for it, but could not find.

S.FORM: mucaan cu maamia kʉkʉnang-ini um-anguru 'inia.
S.PHON: muʦaan ʦu maamia kɨkɨnaŋini umaŋu[r|ɾ]u ʔinia
S.FORM: mucaan cu maamia kʉkʉnangini umanguru 'inia.
S.PHON: muʦaan ʦu maamia kɨkɨnaŋini umaŋu[r|ɾ]u ʔinia
S.TRANSL: Her companions just went away and escaped.
Her companions had just run away.

S.FORM: acu cu ei nimikeinaanu?
S.PHON: aʦu ʦu ei nimikeinaanu
S.FORM: acu cu ei nimikeinaanu?
S.PHON: aʦu ʦu ei nimikeinaanu
S.TRANSL: And then?

TRANSL.notes: Tsuchida (2003) original free translation (OFTE line); I don't know.

S.TRANSL: What happened then?

S.FORM: nguaci cu isua sua tavara.
S.PHON: ŋuaʦi ʦu isua sua tava[r|ɾ]a
S.FORM: nguaci cu isua sua tavara.
S.PHON: ŋuaʦi ʦu isua sua tava[r|ɾ]a
S.TRANSL: Only this is what is known.
That is all that is known.
